docs.title: Memetics
docs.text:
Dependabot watches your dependency versions. Memetics watches your dependency ideas — the implementation patterns you borrowed from somewhere, wrote your own version of, and now have no way of knowing have drifted.

You describe one bit of functionality in a small Markdown file: what it is, optionally a diagram or screenshot, and where it came from upstream — one repo, or several, if it's the same idea reimplemented across frameworks. Memetics runs on a schedule, checks whether anything at those upstream locations has changed since it last looked, and if so, asks Claude to draft a PR updating your local implementation to match — complete with a summary of what changed and why.

flowchart LR
    A[.memetics/*.md files] -->|scheduled run| B[GitHub Action]
    B -->|checks last_seen vs HEAD| C{Upstream changed?}
    C -->|no| D[Exit — nothing to do]
    C -->|yes| E[Fetch old/new file content]
    E --> F[Claude drafts updated local files]
    F --> G[peter-evans/create-pull-request]
    G --> H[PR opened for review]

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• Dependabot updates the library. Nothing updates the code you wrote because of the library. If you reimplemented a pattern instead of importing it — for license reasons, to adapt it to your framework, or because it was simpler than adding a dependency — Dependabot has nothing to bump. Memetics tracks the pattern itself.
  • One pattern, many upstreams. The same idea might exist in two frameworks you watch (e.g. react-window and @tanstack/virtual for virtual scrolling). A meme file can track either, or both.
  • The LLM writes the diff, not just a notification. Instead of "upstream changed, go look," you get an actual PR with the adaptation already drafted against your code's existing style.

docs.text:

docs.title: Meme file format
docs.text:
A meme file is one Markdown file per tracked pattern, living under .memetics/ (any nesting depth — the default scan glob is .memetics/**/*.md). It has YAML frontmatter for the machine-readable tracking state, and a Markdown body for the human- (and Claude-) readable description.

---
upstream:
  - repo: owner/upstream-repo
    paths:
      - src/the/tracked/file.ts
    ref: main
    last_seen: a1b2c3d4e5f6...
local:
  paths:
    - src/your/local-implementation.ts
---

# Pattern name

Free-form description. Include images, rationale, adaptation notes — anything
that helps a future reader (or Claude, when it drafts the update) understand
*why* the local version looks the way it does.

docs.title: upstream (required, list)
docs.text:
One entry per upstream source. A pattern can track one upstream (a 1:1 port of a specific implementation) or several (the same idea, watched across multiple frameworks — Memetics reconciles against whichever one actually changed).

Field Required Description repo yes owner/name on GitHub. paths yes List of file paths within that repo to watch. The most recent commit touching any of them is used as the upstream "version." ref no (default main) Branch, tag, or ref to track. last_seen yes (may be null) The last commit SHA Memetics diffed against. Set to null on first write — the first run records the current HEAD without generating a diff, since there's nothing to compare yet. Memetics updates this field in place after every successful sync; commit the updated file.

docs.title: local (required, object)
docs.text: Field Required Description paths yes List of local files that implement this pattern. These are the files Claude is given as context and allowed to rewrite.

docs.title: Body (Markdown)
docs.text:
Everything after the closing --- is free-form Markdown, passed to Claude verbatim as the "pattern description." Use it for:

  • What the pattern is and why you reimplemented it instead of depending on it directly (license, framework mismatch, simplicity).
  • Diagrams or screenshots — reference images the same way you would in any Markdown file (![caption](./diagram.png)). Keep images alongside the meme file.
  • Adaptation notes — anything that should survive an upstream change: "keep this API stable even if upstream's internals change," "we only support the fixed-size variant," etc. This is the single highest-leverage thing you can write, since it's what keeps Claude's generated update from drifting away from decisions you made on purpose.

docs.title: A note on last_seen: null
docs.text: Setting last_seen: null means "start tracking from here" rather than "diff against empty." On the first run, Memetics records the current upstream commit as the baseline and does not generate a PR — there is no "before" to diff against yet. Every run after that compares real history.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Memetics ships as a single composite GitHub Action (action.yml + scan_and_update.py). It does detection and drafting only — PR creation is left to peter-evans/create-pull-request, a battle-tested action already trusted for exactly this job, rather than reinventing git/PR plumbing.

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Schedule (cron)
    participant A as memetics action
    participant GH as GitHub API (upstream repo)
    participant C as Claude
    participant PR as peter-evans/create-pull-request

    S->>A: trigger
    A->>A: glob .memetics/**/*.md
    loop each meme file
        A->>GH: latest commit touching tracked paths
        alt unchanged since last_seen
            A->>A: skip
        else changed
            A->>GH: fetch old + new file content
            A->>C: pattern description + diff + local files
            C->>A: updated local file(s) + summary
            A->>A: write files, advance last_seen
        end
    end
    A->>PR: changed=true, summary
    PR->>PR: open PR with the diff

docs.title: 1. Discovery
docs.text: The action globs for meme files (default .memetics/**/*.md, configurable via the paths input) and parses each one's YAML frontmatter — see file format.

docs.title: 2. Change detection
docs.text: For each upstream entry, it calls GET /repos/{repo}/commits?path=...&sha=<ref> for every tracked path and takes the most recent commit across all of them. If that SHA matches last_seen, nothing happened — move on. This is a single REST call per tracked path, so a meme file with a handful of upstream paths costs a handful of API calls, no cloning required.

docs.title: 3. Diffing
docs.text: When the latest SHA differs from last_seen, the action fetches the tracked file's content at both the old and new SHA (GET /repos/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref=...) and compares them. A commit can touch a path without changing a specific file (e.g. unrelated changes in the same directory with a path filter that's too broad) — those are detected and skipped so they don't trigger a no-op PR.

docs.title: 4. Drafting the update
docs.text:
If there's a real diff, the action builds one prompt containing:

  • the meme file's Markdown body (the human-authored description and adaptation notes),
  • the upstream before/after content for every changed path,
  • the current content of every file listed under local.paths.

It asks Claude for a structured response (output_config.format with a JSON schema: a list of {path, content} files to write, plus a one-paragraph summary) — not free text to parse. The model is instructed to change only what the upstream diff actually motivates, and to respect the pattern description's own constraints (e.g. "keep this API stable").

docs.title: 5. Writing the result
docs.text: Each returned file is written to disk at its given path, and the meme file's last_seen is advanced to the new SHA — whether or not Claude produced changes, so a path that merely got touched (no real diff) doesn't get re-checked forever.

docs.title: 6. Opening the PR
docs.text: The action's changed output gates a peter-evans/create-pull-request step in the consumer's own workflow, using the action's summary output as the PR body. The actual commit, branch, and PR creation are handled by that action — Memetics never touches git directly.

docs.title: Why an LLM-authored diff instead of just a notification
docs.text: A plain "upstream changed, go check" notification still requires a human to re-derive the adaptation from scratch every time. Memetics instead gives Claude the same context a human would gather by hand — the diff, the original rationale, the current code — and lets it draft the mechanical part of the update. The PR is still reviewed by a human before merge; the value is turning "notice drift" into "evaluate a draft," not full automation.

docs.title: 1. Add an Anthropic API key
docs.text: Memetics calls Claude to draft the update. Add an API key as a repo secret: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret, named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

docs.title: 2. Describe a pattern
docs.text:
Create .memetics/<slug>.md in your repo:

---
upstream:
  - repo: owner/upstream-repo
    paths:
      - path/to/tracked/file.ts
    ref: main
    last_seen: null
local:
  paths:
    - src/your/local-implementation.ts
---

# What this pattern is

A short description of the functionality and why it's implemented this way.
Include a screenshot or diagram if that helps a human (or Claude) understand
the shape of the thing.

last_seen: null means "I haven't checked yet" — the first run will record the current upstream commit without generating a diff (there's nothing to diff against yet), then every run after that compares against it.

docs.title: 3. Add the workflow
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/memetics.yml
name: Memetics sync
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1' # every Monday at 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - id: memetics
        uses: GeorgePearse/memetics@main
        with:
          anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}

      - uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6
        if: steps.memetics.outputs.changed == 'true'
        with:
          title: 'Memetics: sync with upstream changes'
          body: ${{ steps.memetics.outputs.summary }}
          branch: memetics/auto-sync
          commit-message: 'Sync with upstream pattern changes (memetics)'
          labels: memetics

docs.title: 4. Test it without waiting for Monday
docs.text:
Trigger it manually from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch), or from the CLI:

gh workflow run memetics.yml

If nothing in .memetics/ has an upstream change since its recorded last_seen, the action exits cleanly with changed=false and no PR step runs.
